inputs.text: Five months after the ceasefire was announced, people in Gaza are still facing airstrikes, gunfire and shelling, and fishermen are still coming under fire at sea. That is not meaningful peace: civilians remain exposed to violence, while displacement has taken away homes and the livelihoods people need to survive. The language of “normality” cannot cover up who is bearing the cost. Protecting people and enabling them to rebuild must come before political claims of progress—and those with power must be held accountable for making that protection real.
